title: Survey of English Dialects — Wikipedia
content: The Survey of English Dialects was a survey of the dialects of English in England... fieldwork conducted between 1950 and 1961 under the direction of Harold Orton... 313 localities were selected, spread out across England.

citations.used_for: PRIOR — base rate of 'wearside_sunderland_castletown' as the speaker-origin localization within the universe of UK regional-English accent origins resolvable against the Survey of English Dialects (SED) reference corpus. NO published probability exists. The SED reference space comprises ~313 sampled localities across England (Orton fieldwork 1950–1961); Castletown/Southwick on Wearside is a single micro-locality within the Sunderland conurbation. A diffuse, uninformed prior over that locality space is on the order of 1/313 ≈ 0.0032. This figure is a reasoned uniform allocation over the SED locality count, NOT a measured base rate of any accent-origin sampling frame — so it is direction_only, not root-grounded primary data. Real audio-corpus base rates would be skewed by sampling, and no source publishes them.->wearside_sunderland_castletown
